title: Urgent problems: what to do
lead: General first steps while you arrange care. Call the clinic during opening hours; outside them, or for anything serious, go to the nearest hospital emergency department.
hospitalWarning: Go to a hospital emergency department straight away for difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling spreading to the eye or neck, a serious injury, a fit, a child who is floppy or hard to wake, or sudden loss of vision. Do not wait for a clinic appointment.

situations.title: A tooth has been knocked out
steps: Pick it up by the white biting part only; avoid touching the root.
If it is dirty, rinse it briefly in milk or clean water; do not scrub it.
Keep it moist in milk or inside the cheek (adults only) and come to the clinic as quickly as you can.

situations.title: Toothache with swelling
steps: Holding something cold against the cheek, wrapped in a cloth, may help the swelling settle.
Do not put painkiller tablets against the gum.
Book the first available dental slot; go to hospital if swelling spreads or you have a high fever.

situations.title: A denture has cracked
steps: Keep the pieces together in a clean box.
Avoid glue from a shop: it can damage the denture and your gums.
Bring the pieces to the clinic for repair.

situations.title: A child has a high fever
steps: Keep them lightly dressed and offer frequent sips of fluid.
Give fever medicine only at the dose a doctor has advised for their weight.
Babies under three months with a fever, or children who are very drowsy, breathing fast or not drinking, need urgent care.

situations.title: Something has gone into the eye
steps: For chemicals, keep rinsing for several minutes and go to hospital. For anything stuck in the eye or a cut, cover lightly and go to hospital.

situations.title: Chest pain or sudden weakness
steps: This is an emergency: go to the nearest hospital immediately or call 108.
